title: Resistance Training Volume Enhances Muscle Hypertrophy but Not Strength in Trained Men
key_findings: 1, 3 or 5 sets per exercise per session, three sessions a week for 8 weeks, gave similar gains in squat and bench press 1RM and in upper-body muscular endurance.
Muscle growth favoured the higher-volume groups at the elbow flexors, mid-thigh and lateral thigh.
The authors conclude that strength can be gained with short sessions, while hypertrophy rose with volume in this sample.
methods: Randomized trial of three volume conditions (1, 3 or 5 sets per exercise per session), 3 sessions per week on non-consecutive days for 8 weeks; 1RM squat and bench press, bench press repetitions at 50% of 1RM, and ultrasound muscle thickness at four sites.
limitations: Small groups (11 to 12 men each), men only, 8 weeks, and muscle size measured by ultrasound at selected sites.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
